To find which two consecutive whole numbers $\sqrt{57}$ lies between, we first identify the perfect squares that are just below and just above $57.$

The perfect squares closest to $57$ are $49$ and $64.$ We have

$$
49<57<64.
$$

Taking the square root of each number, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{49} & <\sqrt{57}<\sqrt{64} \\ 7 & <\sqrt{57}<8.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14185481/assets/2b5ce9c24d223674d04686a577347e43cd40728194596e75df7c0faa006d2888.png)

This means that $\sqrt{57}$ lies between the consecutive whole numbers $7$ and $8.$ 

Therefore, since $a<b,$ we have $a=7$ and $b=8.$
